profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting for an ML research group preparing the camera-ready version and code release package of a paper comparing pipeline versus end-to-end neural data-to-text generation from RDF triples. The existing proposal under review is the evaluation and release plan: which experiments, tables, and artifacts are considered sufficient to claim the design is reproducible and review-ready. The agenda is to assess whether the current evaluation package covers the needed ablations, qualitative examples, and release artifacts, identify any gaps, and decide what modifications are required before sign-off. The expected outcome is a shared decision on whether the design is ready for internal approval and what final edits or runs should be added.

members.name: Dr. Elena Varga
members.expertise: NLG evaluation, structured data generation, research methodology
members.background: Elena leads a university NLP lab and has published extensively on controllable and modular text generation, often emphasizing careful experimental framing and reviewer-proof evaluation packages.
members.private_state: She wants the paper to pass internal review this week so the team can freeze the camera-ready materials, and she is especially concerned about avoiding reviewer comments that the comparison is incomplete or the release package is hard to use.
hidden_assumptions: When a model variant is described as the 'final model', it refers to the checkpoint selected after the dev-set sweep and averaged across three random seeds, because that is the lab's standard for results tables.

A 'reproducible release' means code, preprocessing scripts, exact split files, and a single command that recreates the paper's main tables; environment containerization is helpful but not essential if the commands run from the repository README.

The 'generalization section' refers specifically to the unseen RDF-combination split described in the latest draft, since that is the only out-of-distribution condition she considers central to the paper's claim.
If the team says the qualitative examples are 'covered', that means one curated appendix page per architecture family, not an exhaustive failure taxonomy.

members.name: Noah Kim
members.expertise: ML systems, experiment infrastructure, model training pipelines, reproducibility tooling
members.background: Noah built the training and evaluation stack for the project, including the RDF preprocessing pipeline, experiment trackers, and release repository, and he often translates research plans into executable artifacts.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid reopening expensive training runs and hopes to define 'ready' in a way that lets him package the repository with minimal rework, while still appearing fully aligned with the paper's scientific goals.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the 'final model', they mean the single best checkpoint from the production run recorded in Weights & Biases, because that is what can actually be restored and shipped cleanly.

A 'reproducible release' means a pinned Docker image plus exported predictions and evaluation outputs; exact regeneration of every reported number from scratch is unrealistic for external users and not necessary for sign-off.

The 'generalization section' includes both the unseen RDF-combination split and the low-resource split added for the workshop talk, since both are already grouped under generalization in his internal dashboards.
If qualitative analysis is 'covered', then a folder of sampled outputs and metric-linked examples is sufficient, even if the appendix only shows a few handpicked cases.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to report and release the 'final model' for each architecture.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the seed-averaged result and the representative checkpoint chosen from the dev-selected sweep that corresponds to the numbers in the paper tables.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the single best restorable checkpoint from the main tracked run for each architecture, even if the paper number came from averaging multiple seeds.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML research meetings, 'final model' is a routine phrase that usually feels settled by context; both think the other is using the lab's normal shorthand, so neither expects clarification to be needed.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether the current package is enough for the 'generalization section'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is talking only about the unseen RDF-combination split that directly supports the paper's claim that pipeline models generalize better to unseen inputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes both the unseen RDF-combination split and the low-resource transfer setting because both sit under a broader internal bucket of generalization experiments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same broad label and both experiments are plausibly about generalization, so surface agreement sounds natural and competent rather than ambiguous.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the repository should be 'reproducible' before approval.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes reproducible means an informed researcher can rerun preprocessing and training/evaluation from the repo and regenerate the main paper tables with the provided split files and commands.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes reproducible means users can run a pinned container and obtain the same predictions and scores from shipped checkpoints/artifacts, without necessarily rebuilding every number end-to-end.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Reproducibility is an established virtue in research, and both are positively oriented toward it; the disagreement is about threshold and evidence, not the goal itself, so it hides beneath sincere agreement.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'add the examples'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'add the examples' to support the qualitative analysis.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a manually curated appendix page with matched examples chosen to illustrate discourse planning and content selection differences between pipeline and end-to-end models.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to export automatically sampled outputs with metadata from the evaluation script and place them in the repo or supplement, assuming that satisfies the request.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view examples as a supporting artifact rather than a first-order design decision; saying 'add the examples' sounds operationally clear even though one imagines editorial curation and the other imagines script-based export.

I want a clean yes-or-no on whether the current evaluation and release plan is sufficient, with only minor edits left.
